Does -- is the witness in any way involved and does he have any knowledge of the documents mentioned?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President I have one question that I'm about to put to the witness that I hope will wrap all that up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's hear it, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall receiving any of this information at or about the time this report was written, sir? Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD JOSEPH [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this point, I can't recall that. That is a factor of memory after 12 years. I simply don't recall it and have the same caution that I mentioned with respect to memory of events concerning allegations about the Armija. I just don't have the recollection now.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. I want to show you another document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you could give us the 65 ter numbers, if you refer to documents, for record.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes. And Judge Kwon, these particular reports do not have 65 ter numbers. These are documents that we are just using in response to some issues that have been raised on cross-examination. But they've all been disclosed long, long ago, in some cases referred to in particular in the witness statements or in the information reports or in the proofing notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm showing you a document which has been marked ET -- I'm sorry, 04258574. It is a one-page or English translation is a two-page translation of a combat report. If we go to the second page, it's signed by Rajko Kusic. Is that the same Kusic, sir, that you recall meeting?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD JOSEPH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rajko Kusic, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And it's dated 15 July at 1 in the morning. I just want to turn your attention back to the first page, sir. Under the heading UNPROFOR, where it says "Check-point number 2 Boksanica, where the UNPROFOR commander has been located, has been put under the control of our forces. An agreement was reached with him not to attack with the condition that they should not open fire on our battle formation which he accepted with the request to leave his positions where they are, and he would in return provide information on enemy activity and would not call in NATO air force." Now first of all, sir, that first sentence referring to OP 2 being under Serb control, is that consistent with your observations on the ground at the time that you were there?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD JOSEPH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Second, with respect to the information of the Ukrainian commander agreeing to provide information of enemy activity and not to call in NATO air force, have you ever received that information before, sir?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD JOSEPH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Does that information surprise you, sir?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD JOSEPH [Resumed]
utterances.text: We -- I take judgement from the Honourable Judges here. This would -- do you want me to share my impressions, definitive knowledge? What is appropriate for this witness to share with the Court?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The question is a simple one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we can move on, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall the video clip Mr. Josse showed you yesterday with an ICRC jeep and what appeared to be French APCs? I think that you identified that that location looked to you like it was OP 2. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD JOSEPH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And my friend, I think tentatively assumed that the date was 27 July. My question to you is would vehicles waiting to enter into the town of Zepa have to pass through OP 2 first?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD JOSEPH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was -- my understanding was that that was the entry point through to the -- I don't believe that there was another access point.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So is it possible that this footage was taken on the 26th or even on the 25th?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD JOSEPH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. I couldn't be certain as to the date that that footage was taken and that those vehicles were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And sir you were also shown a document in which Colonel Baxter said that many houses were burning, apparently torched by departing Bosnians, and were you asked about whether you were aware of that as being a policy. You answered that you were not. And that you did not see that. Did you ever see or hear of Bosniaks torching their own homes as they -- as they fled their territory?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: At which time frame are you referring the witness to?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President in his time in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In his time in Bosnia, okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Throughout the time that I was in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes. Did you receive reports of Bosniaks torching their own homes?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD JOSEPH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me say, if I can, answer this way, in Zepa, I did not observe any Bosniaks torching their own homes. With respect to other locations, I'm not sure. It was not -- here I'm giving a wider view as based on my experience in there. It was not typically the modus operandi for Bosniaks being forcibly expelled to burn their homes. That was not typically their MO. I can't be categorical and say that it never happened. I would not want to be categorical and say it did not happen but that was not the typical MO. There were other examples I can share with the Court of folks who left and burned their homes behind, but it was not a typical Bosniak or Muslim MO that I was aware. But I cannot be categorical and say that it never happened either.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, finally, sir, your proposed demilitarisation agreement refers to the bombardment of the civilian population. You yourself saw the -- what you had described in the report as being a bombardment starting on the 20th. You were asked some questions by my friend, Madam Fauveau, about reducing the fear of the population. Do you think not bombarding the civilian population of Zepa might have helped reduce the fear that you saw?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD JOSEPH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Undoubtedly.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Thayer? Judge Kwon? Yes, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I must ask you to allow me to put a very brief question and that would be the direction to the last question asked by my learned friend. The question is: At the moment of evacuation, which was between the 25th and the 27th of July, was there any shelling?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Can you answer that question, Mr. Joseph, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Was there any shelling? Doesn't show the transcript here, was -- was there any shelling between?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 25th and 27th of July.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we were there? There was no shelling that on us during that evacuation. I do not recall any shelling. There may have been firing but not any shelling in the town or during that evacuation that I can recall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. So we don't have any further questions for you, Mr. Joseph. On behalf of my colleagues and the Tribunal, I should like to thank you for having --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry just one thing for give me it just occurred to me during the break that earlier Mr. Josse's last question I only had an answer in Serbian, and I just would like to say for the record that I do not consider myself self-deceited or however else you want to phrase it. I just wanted to put that in the record. The answer to his question is no. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you for having come over to give evidence and on behalf of everyone I wish you a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Now, either Mr. McCloskey or Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, two brief items are we have had discussions among the Defence, and we have agreed pursuant to the request of one of the teams to switch the order of two witnesses next week. So Witness 132 will precede witness 139. I'll send out my usual schedule in e-mail this afternoon to confirm, but I wanted to put everybody on notice if everybody wasn't. The second is in connection with our previous request to take the week of the 1st through the 5th of October off, we would kindly ask the Court, this is after consultation with our friends, who are unanimous in joining this request, that we also take the following Monday off, the 8th of October. We have Dean Manning arriving from Australia. We will be on the tail end of another witness who will have been giving extensive testimony and who may not be finished by then. We believe that we will be able to save time if we have that extra day of preparation, it will ultimately result in a more efficient, and we hopeless time consuming, presentation of the evidence if we have that day off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We'll discuss that. We've started discussing, and we just want to make sure that if we grant this break, it's because we too believe that you really need it. So we'll come back with our position sometime next week. Thank you. Have a nice weekend, everybody.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 27th day of August, 2007, at 9.00 a.m. 19 20 21 22 23 24

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.45 p.m.,
